name: Rear Naked Choke
description: The highest percentage submission in BJJ. A blood choke from back control that cuts off both carotid arteries by positioning the forearm across one side of the neck and closing the other side with chest and shoulder pressure.
shortInstruction: Elbow under chin, chest glued to back, remove slack, then squeeze.
summary: The most fundamental No-Gi blood choke from back control — master the hand fight, elbow line, and chest-to-back connection.
whyItWorks: Cuts off both carotid arteries when the choking forearm and the opponent's shoulder close both neck lines.
Requires minimal force when the structure is correct — leverage replaces strength.
Creates a dilemma between protecting the neck and escaping back control.
commonMistakes: Squeezing the arms before the elbow is under the chin.
Losing chest contact to chase the finish.
Using the biceps to crank instead of the forearm to cut.
Adding force before removing all slack.

oneMinuteMode.goal: Finish the RNC from back control with clean structure.
steps: Lock seatbelt and glue chest to their back.
Win the hand fight — peel their defensive hand from the neck.
Slide the choking elbow under the chin line.
Close chest and shoulders to complete the choke.

safetySummary: Tap early on neck cranks — distinguish between a blood choke and a neck crank.
Do not twist or crank the neck to force the finish.
Train with controlled partners and release pressure immediately on tap.
keyCorrections: If it becomes a face crank, the elbow is too high — drop it under the chin.
If they turn into you, chest contact is lost — re-glue sternum to spine.
If your hand gets peeled, switch to a high hand fight near the head.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Back control is the platform, not the finish. Each step — seatbelt, hand fight, elbow line, slack removal — must be completed in sequence before squeezing.

decisionTree.condition: One hand is defending the neck line
decisionTree.action: Isolate the defensive hand with your top arm (high wrist control) while keeping chest glued to their back.

decisionTree.condition: Both hands are defending the neck
decisionTree.action: Switch to body triangle or arm trap to break their defensive shell before re-attacking the neck.
Scoot your hips back, re-establish chest-to-back connection, and attack from the opposite side.

decisionTree.condition: Your choking arm is under the jaw (crank position)
decisionTree.action: Release and re-insert the arm lower — the forearm must cross at the neck midline, not under the jaw.

decisionTree.condition: They peel both hands off the neck
decisionTree.action: Return to seatbelt control, hand fight again — never chase the choke without structure.

exitStrategies: If the choke is consistently blocked, transition to arm traps and attack the armbar or bow-and-arrow.
If they escape to mount bottom, transition to mount control and attack from there.
If they scramble out, re-attack with a front headlock or guillotine as they face you.

moneyDetails: The elbow-under-chin detail is everything — without it, you have a crank, not a choke.
Chest-to-back contact freezes their escape before you even squeeze.
Removing slack is more important than squeezing hard.
nextStep: After finishing the RNC or if it fails, chain into arm traps, mount transition, or back take re-entry.
fixItFast: Can't find the neck line? Switch to the other arm or create more angle by walking your hips.
Getting peeled? Tuck your chin and switch to high wrist control.
Lost chest contact? Reconnect before squeezing — without it, they will escape.
